findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin the exact header/body boundary for the relocation comment (e.g. header line + single `\n` + verbatim body with no added/stripped trailing newline) and state how 'comment body minus header' is extracted, so the AC1 byte-exact diff is deterministically satisfiable.
evidence: Step 1: 'whose first line is `Relocated from docs/<file> ...`, followed by the file body verbatim.'
AC1: 'whose body equals the deleted file (verify: diff <(git show ...:<file>) <(comment body minus header) is empty).'

The AC subtracts 'header' but 'header' is defined only as 'first line'; the separator newline(s) and any store-side normalization of the body are unspecified, so the empty-diff gate may fail even on a correct relocation.
findings.finding: AC1's byte-exact verification (`diff <(git show 083620b08116:docs/<file>) <(comment body minus header)` is empty) is load-bearing but under-specifies the header/body boundary: the plan does not state how many newlines separate the 'Relocated from ...' first line from the verbatim body, nor whether comment_ticket stores the body without trailing-whitespace/newline normalization — the diff is sensitive to both.
findings.location: Approach step 1 and Acceptance Criteria AC1
scenarios: The comment store appends or strips a trailing newline, or the author inserts a blank line between header and body, making the byte diff non-empty for a faithful relocation and blocking acceptance.
